nodes.rationale: The Seleccionados sheet is no longer overwritten on regeneration so manual promotions from the waitlist and payment tracking are preserved across re-runs of the evaluation.

nodes.label: TSV Double-Escape Column Bug Fix
nodes.rationale: A double-escaped \t caused column count mismatch during Seleccionados sheet restoration; fixed by correcting the escape handling.

nodes.label: Corrección de Puntajes (Score Correction)
nodes.rationale: Extra whitespace in CONFIG.COLUMNS column-name constants caused silent loss of Disponibilidad and Compromiso scores; fixed by trimming/normalizing column names.

nodes.label: Migración de Monolito JS a TypeScript Modular
nodes.rationale: Migrated from a 1.6k-line JavaScript monolith to a modular TypeScript architecture with strict typing for maintainability.

nodes.label: GSD Meta-Prompting Philosophy
nodes.rationale: GSD treats every file as both implementation and specification; files teach the AI how to build software systematically, optimizing for solo developer + AI workflow, deliberate context engineering, and plans as executable prompts.

nodes.label: Fresh Context Pattern
nodes.rationale: Spawned subprocesses get only the specific plan and minimal necessary context, never accumulated orchestrator state, to keep quality high.

nodes.label: SPEC → PLAN → EXECUTE → VERIFY → COMMIT Protocol
nodes.norm_label: spec → plan → execute → verify → commit protocol

nodes.label: Planning Lock
nodes.rationale: No implementation code may be written until SPEC.md is marked Status: FINALIZED, preventing premature coding against unstable requirements.

nodes.label: Search-First Discipline
nodes.rationale: Searching before reading full files reduces context pollution, speeds understanding, and prevents reading irrelevant code.

nodes.label: Model Independence Rule
nodes.rationale: No rule, workflow, or skill may hard-depend on a specific model provider; adapters offer optional provider-specific enhancements only, so GSD keeps working if a given model is unavailable.

nodes.label: Auto-Save Protocol
nodes.rationale: Sessions can terminate abruptly (usage limits, context limits, network errors); saving state before recommending /pause ensures state persists even if the agent never gets to finish the handoff.

nodes.label: User = Reporter, AI = Investigator
nodes.rationale: The user only reports symptoms (expected vs actual behavior, error messages); the AI must investigate the cause itself rather than asking the user to diagnose.

nodes.label: Meta-Debugging Own Code
nodes.rationale: Debugging code you wrote is harder because design decisions feel obviously correct and memory of intent can diverge from what was actually implemented; treat your own code as foreign and question it.

nodes.label: Forbidden Completion Phrases
nodes.rationale: Phrases like 'this should work' or 'the code looks correct' are banned as justification for completion because they substitute belief for empirical proof.

nodes.label: Execution Flow (Load State → Load Plan → Determine Pattern → Execute Tasks)

nodes.label: Task Commit Protocol (one task = one commit)
nodes.norm_label: task commit protocol (one task = one commit)

nodes.label: Need-to-Know Context Loading
nodes.rationale: Fresh context beats accumulated context; only the plan being executed and current state should be loaded, never all previous summaries or full architecture docs.

nodes.label: Solo Developer + AI Workflow Philosophy
nodes.rationale: Plans are written for one person (visionary/product owner) and one implementer (the AI) — no teams, stakeholders, or ceremonies; effort is estimated in AI execution time, not human dev time.

nodes.label: Plans Are Prompts Principle
nodes.rationale: PLAN.md is not transformed into a prompt — it IS the prompt, containing objective, context, tasks with verification, and success criteria, executed directly.

nodes.label: Optimization Strategies (progressive loading, JIT, search-before-load, summarize)

nodes.label: Trust Nothing, Verify Everything
nodes.rationale: SUMMARY.md claims of completion, existing code, called functions, and passing tests must all be independently verified rather than trusted at face value.
